id: title:Gilbert09:force virtual hosted s3 addressing without a proxy

review.posthog_relevance: Warehouse ingestion compatibility and operational stability
review.reason: The change P1.F1.H4 explicitly modifies warehouse ingestion configuration to use virtual-hosted S3 addressing and bypasses the egress proxy for warehouse buckets, preventing potential 403 errors and compatibility issues with S3-compatible storage. P1.F2.H1 adds regression tests for this behavior. This represents a substantive, bounded improvement in the reliability and correctness,
review.uncertainty: No adoption or incident avoidance data is available; the benefit is inferred solely from the compatibility and configuration changes.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single-file change group. No other PRs are supplied, so no cross-PR relationship can be established. No tier assignment is performed.

observations.behavior: Adds virtual-hosted S3 addressing and scoped egress-proxy bypass; the addressing style is now forced independently of the proxy bypass, while the proxy bypass remains scoped to the warehouse bucket hostname.
observations.posthog_connection: PostHog warehouse ingestion uses S3-compatible storage; this change prevents 403 errors against S3-compatible stores that require virtual-hosted addressing, while keeping warehouse traffic off the configured egress proxy. observations.behavior: Adds a new test for the regression where addressing style is forced even without a proxy, and a new test for dotted bucket names. These checks the behavior demonstrated in P1.F1.H4.
observations.posthog_connection: These checks support the regression prevention and dotted-bucket exception. No tier is assigned.
